s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and evolving left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
Inducible angina at 50 W without ECG changes
Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis with in-stent restenosis
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
New QTc prolongation to 500 ms and severely reduced LVEF of 35%
key_facts: 67-year-old man with hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Normal sinus rhythm on admission
Q waves in lead III and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF on ECG
Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities on initial echocardiography
Patent stents in the circumflex artery and non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery on coronary angiography
Worsening chest pain after transfer to the intensive care unit
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 on ECG after worsening chest pain
Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch on second angiogram
Successful treatment with balloon angioplasty
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and echocardiography results are consistent with this condition, including akinesia of all apical segments and severely reduced LVEF

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with worsening chest pain and ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, which are indicative of myocardial infarction

shortlist.label: Stent thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of percutaneous coronary interventions and presented with worsening chest pain, which could be related to stent thrombosis

shortlist.label: Vasospastic angina
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including worsening chest pain and ST-segment elevation, could be related to vasospastic angina

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed QTc prolongation to 500 ms after recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, which is a risk factor for this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and subsequent development of akinesia of all apical segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% after a stressful event is consistent with takotsubo syndrome, also known as stress cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The patient had patent stents and no significant disease in major arteries, and the echocardiography changes were not typical of a myocardial infarction

rejected.label: Stent thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient's stents were patent, and the issue was with a subocclusion of a branch, not the stent itself

rejected.label: Vasospastic angina
rejected.why: While the patient had chest pain and ST-segment elevation, the subsequent development of severe left ventricular dysfunction is not typical of vasospastic angina

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's QTc prolongation to 500 ms was a new finding after the cardiac event, and the primary issue was the cardiomyopathy, not a primary electrical disorder
